title: TensorTransit raw frontier result
description: One measured configuration, in one workload cell, on one repeat, for one variant. Deliberately the finest grain the runner produces: a receipt whose inputs were reduced before they were stored cannot be re-scored when the evaluator is fixed, and re-scoring is the only honest way to correct an evaluator bug.

provenance.description: Everything a receipt needs to say what was measured. No prompt, no token, no request body: a raw result records rates and latencies, and there is nowhere in this schema to put application data.

workload_id.description: A cell the generation declares. A cell it does not declare has no published weight, and inventing one is how a hidden priority gets in.

config_id.description: Which allowed configuration of that variant produced this point. A cell's frontier is formed from all of them.

repeat.description: Paired: repeat k of main and repeat k of the candidate ran adjacently on one box.

metrics.description: Raw units. Only the objectives the generation declares are scored; anything else here is diagnostic, and a diagnostic can never move a score.

status.description: Anything other than OK produces NO operating point. A failure is the absence of a point, not a slow one: normalizing an OOM into a small positive score would let a lost operating region still contribute hypervolume.

attribution.description: Only on a record whose status is a SERVING guard. Who the loss belongs to. `runtime` means the evaluator re-ran the cell on the BASELINE binary with the hook installed and no window and reproduced the failure, so the cell is not scored and the receipt names it. `unresolved` is the default and keeps the loss with the candidate.
